crime: When {WITCH_NAME} was a child, her classmates tipped her pencil case onto the classroom floor, and pebbles rolled out. "Why would a girl carry rocks?" The whole class laughed.
In the prison she walked the lake shore alone, choosing stones by their weight in her palm. Each one she kept, she touched and pictured as a bar of soap, and everyone saw soap.

Another prisoner, a girl with a sketchbook, went down to that shore an hour before sunset every evening to draw it, and at supper she always handed {WITCH_NAME} the page first. One evening in the dining hall, she passed round a new sunset. On the shore in the picture stood {WITCH_NAME}, holding a stone up to the light. "The most beautiful thing I saw today," the artist said.
The other prisoners laughed and asked {WITCH_NAME} to show them her rocks. The artist promised to draw one of those stones for the table every night.

Before sunset, on the shore, {WITCH_NAME} chose a stone by its weight in her palm and struck the artist on the temple. Then she touched the sketchbook and pictured a finished sunset on its blank page, in the artist's own line. From before sunset until the search, she sat among the girls in the lounge.

The prisoners found the artist on the shore, her sketchbook open on a finished sunset, a pencil still in her fingers. In the trial court they reasoned she had been struck just after finishing it, while {WITCH_NAME} sat with them.
Then one prisoner pointed to the side of the dead girl's drawing hand. It was clean. Every evening it had come to supper grey.
She had died before sunset, they realized, over a blank page {WITCH_NAME} had dressed as a drawing.
fields.epitaph: Once she stood in the light undisguised, and someone called her beautiful.
fields.epithet: Keeper of Stones Dressed as Soap
execution: The execution stand raises an iron spindle beneath a great roll of plain grey paper, and she is bound upright to it. The spindle turns. The paper winds around her, layer over layer, climbing up across her face. When the spindle stops turning, all that is left is a smooth grey parcel that no longer stirs. An iron hand sets it on a shelf of identical grey parcels, and no one can tell which one is her.

magic.name: Masquerade
magic.text: Anything she touches can look, to everyone, like any other object she pictures.
